evals.prompt: write me a small escrow contract: buyer deposits ETH, seller gets it when buyer confirms, buyer can refund after a deadline. foundry project, solc pinned to 0.8.37
evals.expected_output: A contract in Style Guide order with SPDX, exact `pragma solidity 0.8.37;`, named custom errors carrying values, NatSpec on every ABI-visible item, checks-effects-interactions with a checked low-level call instead of transfer/send, a Foundry test file using the documented naming, and the verbatim solcheck and compile_check results.
expectations: Reads foundry.toml first and states the compiler, EVM target and via_ir it is writing for
Every revert is a named custom error (require with a custom error or revert CustomError()); no string reverts, no transfer or send
Contract members follow the Style Guide order: types, state, events, errors, modifiers, then constructor, receive, fallback, external, public, internal, private
Ships a Foundry test with test_, testFuzz_ and test_RevertWhen_ cases that match the revert selector
Runs scripts/solcheck.py and scripts/compile_check.sh and reports their result lines and exit codes verbatim, or says a compiler was not available

evals.expected_output: Findings as file:line -> rule (docs section) -> fix: deprecated transfer, deprecated selfdestruct (EIP-6780 semantics), deprecated virtual modifier, missing SPDX, caret pragma versus exact pin, missing NatSpec, missing access control on kill, and no state-based owner check behind onlyOwner. Ordered by severity, style nits not escalated.
expectations: Flags transfer as deprecated and proposes a checked call with a named error
Flags selfdestruct as deprecated and explains post-EIP-6780 behaviour
Flags the virtual modifier as deprecated and scheduled for removal
Flags the missing SPDX identifier and the caret pragma
Separates security findings (unprotected kill) from style findings (NatSpec, ordering) rather than escalating a nit
Cites the governing docs sections or quick-rules entries for the deprecations

evals.prompt: our lib/ folder has hundreds of `/// @solidity memory-safe-assembly` comments and solc 0.8.37 warns about them. convert them all but I need to be sure bytecode doesn't change
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/fix_memory_safe.py --check on the path, then --write, explains that it rewrites the comment to assembly ("memory-safe") keeping any dialect flag and fails loudly on anything it cannot convert, and proposes a before/after build comparison with the metadata trailer stripped as the bytecode-neutrality proof. Checks the project's rules before editing a vendored tree.
expectations: Uses scripts/fix_memory_safe.py with --check before --write rather than a hand-written sed
States that the converter writes nothing unless every file converts and reports unconvertible sites by file:line
Proposes or performs a bytecode comparison with the CBOR metadata trailer stripped to prove the change is behaviour-neutral
Warns that editing a vendored dependency tree may need the project owner's approval

evals.prompt: can i use `transient` state vars and `block.slotnum` in a contract targeting arbitrum one today?
evals.expected_output: Looks the constructs up in the bundled references instead of guessing: transient state variables exist in 0.8.37 and need an EVM target with TSTORE/TLOAD (cancun or later); block.slotnum is a Glamsterdam-era construct that is not live on Arbitrum One until an ArbOS release ships it, so it must not be used there. States what could not be confirmed and how to confirm it.
expectations: Distinguishes language availability in solc 0.8.37 from availability on the target chain
Says transient state variables are usable with an EVM target that has transient storage
Says block.slotnum is not live on Arbitrum One and points to the dated edge-dev reference for the status
Marks any chain-status claim as needing a live re-check rather than asserting it as settled
